clue.text: Winner of the Wingate prize for cake

annotationWithheld.why: Winner of the Wingate prize for cake (6): PARKIN fits 'cake' and every crossing, but no Wingate Prize winner of that name can be confirmed, so the first definition is unparsed
annotationWithheld.clue: Winner of the Wingate prize for cake

clue.text: Play safe, knock

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
pan means criticise harshly, to knock

explanation.surface: Advice to take no risks, then a knock at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play safe' reads as a phrase, but 'Play' is the definition and 'safe' the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is J. M. Barrie's 1904 stage drama about the boy who never grows up.

clue.text: A satirist artist is screening The Third Man

indicators.note: screening means the artist shields another piece inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Abel was the third man in Genesis, after Adam and Cain
is as written

explanation.surface: A satirical artist is showing the film The Third Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Third Man' looks like the Graham Greene film, but here it means the third man in Genesis; 'screening' hides him inside the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the French Renaissance writer of the satirical Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: First of Israelite leaders from Sarah and Abraham combined

definitions.text: First of Israelite leaders from Sarah and Abraham combined

indicators.note: First of takes the opening letter of the next word
leaders from takes the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A patriarch born of Sarah and Abraham together, first of the line of Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Isaac was the son of Sarah and Abraham and an early patriarch of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, the child of Sarah and Abraham, is one of the founding patriarchs of the Israelite people.

clue.text: Article by King more than work by Conrad

parts.note: the definite article is the word 'the'
R stands for Rex, Latin for king
over can mean more than, as in 'over fifty'

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by a monarch outshines one of Joseph Conrad's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rover is Joseph Conrad's last completed novel, published in 1923.

clue.text: Head's oration butchered some classical verses

indicators.note: butchered means the speech is hacked about into a new order

parts.note: the letters of 'Head's' as written

explanation.surface: A headmaster's speech mangles some lines of classical poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butchered' rearranges HEADS ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace's Odes are lyric poems in Latin, classical verse of the first century BC.

clue.text: Ex-president's deception, plain to the auditors

indicators.note: to the auditors means as heard by listeners

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or deception; veldt is open grassland, a plain, in southern Africa

explanation.surface: A former president's trickery is obvious to those listening.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' stands for 'is'. 'plain' looks like 'obvious'; it is the noun, VELDT.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Maybe claret that is involving North Virginia in Foreign Affairs

indicators.note: involving means taking another piece inside

parts.note: claret is an example of vin, French for wine
ie abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Claret involved in diplomatic dealings in North Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign Affairs' looks like diplomacy; it is Alison Lurie's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinnie Miner, properly Virginia, is the heroine of Alison Lurie's novel Foreign Affairs.

clue.text: Semi-literary, it is in something exceptional

indicators.note: is in means one piece goes inside the other
Semi- means only half of the word is kept, its first half removed

parts.note: it as written

explanation.surface: A half-literate effort that is somehow remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi-' keeps only the second half of the word, and 'is in' places the pronoun inside that half.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is an uncommon or outstanding thing.

clue.text: Against prejudice, like Smollett

parts.note: to can mean against, as in leaning a ladder to the wall
bias is a synonym of prejudice

explanation.surface: A novelist praised for being free of prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against prejudice' reads as 'opposed to bias', but it is simply TO + BIAS run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist Smollett's first name was Tobias, so the answer shares his given name.

clue.text: War poet sounded close to ousting a novelist, Anita

indicators.note: sounded tells us the poet's surname is taken by its spoken form

parts.note: Rupert Brooke was the best-known poet of the First World War

indicators.note: ousting means the named letter is thrown out of the word for close

parts.note: near means close, as in 'close by'
the letter a as written

explanation.surface: A war poet edges a novelist out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: BROOKE said aloud gives BROOK; NEAR with its A ousted gives NER.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita Brookner was the English novelist who won the Booker Prize for Hotel du Lac.

clue.text: Invisible Man author hip loners all found moving

indicators.note: moving means the letters shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: A novelist's book has hip loners touched by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link; 'moving' rearranges HIP LONERS ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Ellison's Invisible Man (1952) is a landmark novel of the Black American experience.

clue.text: Unenthusiastic about books, including a cult novel

indicators.note: including means the scrambled letters sit within the other two pieces

parts.note: re means about or concerning
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone lukewarm about reading, a cult novel among the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges the letters of 'a cult' to give LUCTA, and 'including' places them between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reluctant means lacking eagerness or willingness, which is being lukewarm.

clue.text: A poet endlessly laboured over

indicators.note: over signals the word is turned round, read back to front
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: toiled means laboured, worked hard

explanation.surface: A poet slaved away over his verses without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TOILED to TOILE, and 'over' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was the poet of The Waste Land and Four Quartets.

clue.text: Noble calls to abandon love for a dramatist

parts.note: aristo is short for aristocrat, a noble

indicators.note: to abandon tells us a letter is dropped from the word for calls
for means the dropped letter is replaced by another one

parts.note: phones as a verb means calls
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
the letter a as written

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's phone calls give up on romance in favour of a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' and 'for' swap the O in PHONES for A, giving PHANES.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes was the comic playwright of ancient Athens, author of The Frogs and Lysistrata.

clue.text: It's a novel about Ireland's blind prophet

indicators.note: about means wrapped around another piece
novel means new, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, with the possessive s kept

explanation.surface: A novel about an Irish seer who cannot see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges IT'S A into TIAS, and 'about' splits it after the T to wrap round Ireland's Irish name.
explanation.definitionFit: Teiresias was the sightless seer of Thebes in Greek myth.

clue.text: Line poorly worded about island, home to a short race

indicators.note: about means wrapped around the next piece

parts.note: ill means poorly, badly
put means worded, as in 'nicely put'

explanation.surface: A badly phrased line about an island where small people live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly worded' reads as an adverb and a past participle meaning badly put, which 'about' wraps round the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilliput in Gulliver's Travels is the island of tiny people.

clue.text: Star visits Paramount about raising capital in South America

indicators.note: visits means one piece goes inside another
raising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: paramount means number one, written NO I
ca abbreviates circa, about
the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A film star visits the Paramount studio while raising money in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' reverses the number-one and circa pieces to ACION, and 'visits' puts the star in after its first letter. Asunción is spelt with an accent in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunción is the capital city of Paraguay.

clue.text: Twin heroines disguised as chivalric heroes

indicators.note: disguised means the letters are dressed up in a different order

explanation.surface: Twin heroines in a romance dress up as knights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' rearranges TWIN HEROINES; 'as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nine Worthies were nine historical and legendary figures held up in the Middle Ages as models of chivalry.

clue.text: Greek wizard services goddesses

parts.note: aces in tennis are winning serves, wizard ones

explanation.surface: A Greek magician serves goddesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wizard' looks like a noun; it is the adjective 'brilliant'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Graces were three sister goddesses of charm and beauty in Greek myth.

clue.text: Japanese verse about a Tiger, helpful to Bond

indicators.note: about means wrapped around another piece

parts.note: a tanka is a short Japanese poem of thirty-one syllables

explanation.surface: A Japanese poem about a tiger that is useful to Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiger' looks like the animal; it is a character's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Tanaka is the Japanese secret service chief who aids Bond in You Only Live Twice.

clue.text: Who wrote of the cloister where a dean entertains?

indicators.note: entertains means the words hold a guest inside them

explanation.surface: A question about which author described monastery life where a dean plays host.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits inside 'where a dean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade wrote The Cloister and the Hearth, a historical novel of 1861.

clue.text: Left boot worn by Len Stephen Gordon's lover, Mary

indicators.note: worn by means one piece is put on, inside, the other

parts.note: the name Len as written
a welly is a wellington, a rubber boot

explanation.surface: A man named Len wears his left boot.
explanation.walkthrough: A WELLY is a British rubber boot (a wellington).
explanation.definitionFit: In Radclyffe Hall's The Well of Loneliness, Mary Llewellyn is the young woman loved by the heroine Stephen Gordon.

clue.text: For one upset girl he's a dream father

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example, for one

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An upset girl thinks her father is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dream father' means a father in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Egeus is Hermia's father in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Epistolary novel central in depicting Zhivago's true love

indicators.note: central in picks out the middle letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Lara in Doctor Zhivago is properly named Larissa

explanation.surface: A novel told in letters, depicting Zhivago's great love at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of DEPICTING is C.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Richardson's Clarissa is told entirely through letters between its characters.

clue.text: Where Pythia served a key character in Greece

parts.note: Del is the delete key on a keyboard
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: The Greek priestess's place of service turns on a key Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pythia was the priestess of Apollo's oracle at the shrine near Mount Parnassus.

clue.text: Maybe Gloria Gaynor's first and last show

parts.note: Gloria Swanson is an example of someone named Gloria, the silent-film star

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the singer's name

explanation.surface: The singer Gloria Gaynor's first and final concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloria Gaynor' looks like one name; it splits into Gloria (Swanson) and Gaynor's first letter. 'and' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a final performance, from the legend that swans sing just before dying.

clue.text: Lucy who wed at Lammermoor in a quiet fashion

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ton means fashion or style, as in 'the height of ton'

explanation.surface: A bride wed quietly and stylishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucy Ashton is the doomed heroine of Walter Scott's The Bride of Lammermoor.
